title: Chapter 98
content:
Torrential rain poured through the shattered windshield, soaking the ruined upholstery.

Staring down the barrels of dozens of assault rifles, Jakyeong was struck speechless. A single twitch of a finger would reduce the car to Swiss cheese. Beside him, Kang Il-hyun sat with an expression devoid of its usual mocking arrogance—his features carved from rigid, arctic stone.

Two heavily armed mercenaries detached from the formation, advancing on the roadster to flank both doors with their weapons raised.

Jakyeong reached for the door handle, but Il-hyun’s hand clamped down hard on his forearm.

"Wait here."

Jakyeong bit his lip. "But—!"

"Do not step out of this vehicle," Il-hyun repeated, his voice dangerously low, "until I give the word."

Faced with that unyielding, absolute command, Jakyeong had no choice but to give a stiff nod.

Il-hyun pushed the mangled driver-side door open and stepped into the deluge. The hit team that had pursued them from the cinema stood shoulder-to-shoulder, forming an impenetrable wall around the Chairman.

With rain plastering his dark hair to his forehead, Il-hyun walked toward the center of the perimeter with slow, measured strides.

Chairman Kang dropped his smoldering cigar into a puddle, greeting his son with eyes as cold as a serpent’s.

"It appears I interrupted a splendid afternoon."

A razor-thin smile pulled at Il-hyun's lips, though his dark pupils were frosted over. "If you knew that, you should have scheduled your intrusion for later."

"Our discussion will likely take quite some time. Wouldn't it be wiser to relocate to a more private setting?"

Il-hyun glanced back over his shoulder.

Through the spiderwebbed glass of the totaled roadster, Lee Ja-kyeong was glaring through the gloom. Il-hyun ground his molars together until the muscles along his jaw ached, then turned back to the patriarch.

"Let the boy go."

"And why should I?"

"Let him walk. I am asking you."

A polite request. Because if they were dragged away together, only two outcomes awaited them: a bullet in the dirt, or a lifetime crippled in a subterranean cell. Chairman Kang hadn't mobilized this much private military muscle without intending to settle the board once and for all. Il-hyun had mistakenly assumed the old beast was cornered and paralyzed by fear; in truth, the cunning old fox had merely been biding his time, waiting for his son to drop his guard.

"He is an accomplice on your board, isn't he?"

"Which is why I am formally asking you to release him."

The Chairman’s wrinkled eyes narrowed into fine slits, a faint, mocking amusement dancing on his lips. "I wonder. Would the young man even accept your charity?"

"I will handle him."

A suffocating silence fell over the desolate highway. The torrential deluge tapered into a fine, gray drizzle, the biting tension dropping the atmospheric pressure below freezing. Il-hyun waited in stillness, maintaining his composure.

The fraction of a second felt like an eternity.

Finally, Chairman Kang gave a microscopic tilt of his chin.

Il-hyun turned on his heel, striding back toward the driver's side to face Jakyeong.

The boy looked visibly rattled, his dark eyes brimming with a chaotic storm of defiance, panic, and—unless Il-hyun’s instincts were playing tricks on him—a distinct trace of raw affection.

It really was an eventful day, Il-hyun thought. An unexpected proposal at dawn, a visit to his childhood home, and an ordinary, beautiful date just like normal people.

For a parting gift before the executioner arrives... it wasn't a bad run.

Reaching through the shattered frame, Il-hyun gently cupped the boy's cheek. Jakyeong didn't flinch away, merely glaring back with unblinking intensity, as if already anticipating the words to come.

"We part ways here, darling."

The muscle beneath Jakyeong’s left eye twitched violently.

"Head back to the estate and wait for me. Once I wrap up this little family dispute with Father, I'll return."

"No."

"I'll be back shortly."

"I said no."

Il-hyun had known the boy wouldn't fold easily, but the sheer stubbornness was maddening. Clamping his jaw into a hard line, Jakyeong reached for the interior handle, attempting to force the door open.

Il-hyun shoved the steel frame shut with his shoulder, his baritone cracking with a rare, desperate edge:

"Please."

Jakyeong gritted his teeth, paralyzed by the sight. It was the very first time he had ever seen genuine panic in Kang Il-hyun's eyes.

Why are you looking at me like that? Smirk at me. Throw a vile, sleazy joke. Act like your usual psychotic self.

To an outsider, the idea of a biological father slaughtering his own heir sounded unthinkable; to Jakyeong, who had been contracted to execute Il-hyun in the first place, the reality was bone-chillingly clear. Walking into the Chairman's custody meant walking straight to the slaughterhouse.

The fingers that had cradled his cheek moved upward, gently smoothing the damp dark hair from his forehead.

"Goodbye, darling."

Offering a soft, lingering smile, Il-hyun turned and walked back toward the Chairman’s motorcade.

Chief Secretary Kim immediately stepped forward with a handheld RF scanner, sweeping Il-hyun’s frame. Detecting the encrypted transponder built into his luxury wristwatch, the secretary made him unbuckle the band, hurled the timepiece onto the asphalt, and put three suppressed rounds through the casing.

Sparks strobed in the dark as the circuitry shattered.

Throughout the process—even as heavy zip-ties bound his wrists behind his back—Il-hyun remained eerily, unnervingly compliant.

Watching from the driver's seat, a sudden spark ignited in Jakyeong’s mind.

While the sentry guarding his door glanced toward the motorcade, Jakyeong slipped his hand into the glove compartment, retrieving an analog burner phone. Keeping his movements concealed beneath the steering column, he popped the plastic backplate, extracted a microscopic GPS transponder chip, and slipped the silicone square onto his tongue.

He swallowed hard. The sharp metal snagged briefly against his esophagus before washing down with saliva.

He cleared his throat, calling out in a quiet rasp: "Hey."

The guard standing two paces away turned his head. Jakyeong whispered something unintelligible, drawing the man closer to the open window.

In a flash of blinding speed, Jakyeong grabbed the guard by the hair, slamming his skull into the door pillar with concussive force. He snatched the dropped sidearm, kicked the door wide, and leveled the weapon straight at the center of Chairman Kang's chest.

The sudden breach instantly drew every laser sight and tactical flashlight onto Jakyeong’s chest.

Turning his head, the remaining color drained from Il-hyun’s face.

Standing in the downpour with his shirt soaked through, Jakyeong held his aim with unwavering discipline.

"You're not taking him!"

His roar echoed across the barren highway.

"Take me with you! Or put us both in the fucking ground right here!"

Il-hyun lunged forward in a blind fury, but a mercenary stepped into his blind spot, driving a heavy rifle stock straight into the back of his skull.

CRACK.

Il-hyun collapsed onto the wet asphalt with a low, agonizing groan.

As he struggled to push himself up, Chairman Kang planted the heavy brass ferrule of his cane into his son's spine, pinning him to the ground. A pool of diluted crimson bloomed across the pavement where Il-hyun's forehead rested.

Jakyeong watched the brutality with bared teeth, his finger trembling against the trigger guard.

Chairman Kang smiled—a cold, demonic smirk that mirrored his son's darkest moments, yet carried an ancient, rotten malice.

"If you insist on joining the party... who am I to refuse?"

The command dropped, and mercenaries swarmed the roadster.

Recognizing that pulling the trigger would only result in an immediate firing squad, Jakyeong allowed the sidearm to slip from his fingers. Heavy hands wrenched his arms behind his back, securing his wrists with zip-ties before yanking a thick canvas hood over his head.

Total, suffocating darkness enveloped him.

A fraction of a second later, a blunt, concussive blow struck the base of his skull.

His knees buckled, and his consciousness began slipping beneath the tide.

Was this a mistake? Did I just throw my life away?

He didn't have the answer. All he knew was that leaving Kang Il-hyun to die alone in the dark was an impossibility he couldn't live with.

Staring out the window of the executive SUV cruising down the palm-lined Hawaiian boulevard, Wang Ryun remained draped in heavy, inconsolable gloom.

No matter how breathtaking the tropical scenery was, the jagged wound left by his lover's betrayal refused to close. To make matters worse, Wang Han had spent the entire transit from the airport clutching his phone with white knuckles, fidgeting like a man on death row.

"Something's wrong," Han muttered for the tenth time.

Ryun let out a lifeless, hollow sigh. "What now?"

"Wei isn't answering. Something happened to him."

Ryun groaned, staring at the floorboards. If anything happened to him, it’s that his back is broken from getting ravished. With Il-hyun’s security detail occupying the front seats, he swallowed the crude remark. Between the private security convoy flanking their rear and the dedicated trauma surgeon flown in purely for his flank, it was obvious the CEO was pathologically obsessed with their younger brother.

"They're probably tangled up in bed right now," Ryun grumbled.

"You think so?"

"That's your fatal flaw, Han-ge. You still treat that lethal bastard like he's ten years old."

"I suppose..."

"Meanwhile, your broken-hearted second brother is sitting right here, entirely invisible."

Han offered a sheepish, apologetic smile at the accusation. It wasn't favoritism, but the significant age gap meant he had practically raised Jakyeong from a bruised, feral orphan into a grown man. The protective instinct was hardwired into his marrow.

Still, the knot in Han's gut refused to loosen. "He has never left my calls unreturned for this long..."

Right then, the encrypted phone in the front passenger seat chimed.

The security lead answered with crisp, military deference, listening for two seconds before passing the handset straight into the back. Han’s heart skipped a beat when he heard Park Tae-soo’s voice—but as the briefing unfolded, the blood drained entirely from his face.

He terminated the call, his skin as white as chalk.

"What is it?" Ryun asked, alarmed.

"Wei... was abducted."

"Wei abducted someone? Who?"

"No, you idiot! He was taken!"

"Stop fucking around."

"It's real! Kang Il-hyun's father mobilized a strike team and took them both!"

"Fuck!"

Ryun bolted upright in his seat, slamming the crown of his head violently against the roof of the SUV.

Lee Ja-kyeong was the kind of apex predator who kidnapped others for a living—he wasn't someone who got hauled away quietly. If he had been captured, the operational board was swimming in blood.

Before the driver could even ask for orders, both brothers roared in unison:

"Turn the car around! Back to the airfield! Now!"

The driver swung the heavy SUV into an aggressive U-turn, coordinating emergency flight clearances with Tae-soo.

Han desperately redialed Jakyeong’s number, but the carrier message continued to drone its dead, automated loop.

The swallowed transponder.

Han had designed that microscopic locator specifically for emergency extractions—built to be ingested and activated via stomach acid—but the satellite signal could only be tracked once they were physically within regional grid range in South Korea.

Hold on, Wei. Just stay alive until we touch down.

Darkness.

Jakyeong’s consciousness slowly surfaced, yet his vision remained locked in a pitch-black void. With every ragged breath, the damp, rough canvas hood pressed against his mouth and nostrils. He attempted to rotate his shoulders, but his wrists were securely bound behind his back with industrial zip-ties.

Without warning, the hood was yanked from his head.

Blinding, raw fluorescent light flooded his eyes.

Panting heavily, Jakyeong squinted through the glare, mapping the perimeter.

An unfamiliar location. Unfamiliar faces.

He was inside a concrete industrial structure—an abandoned, half-finished construction site with the entire eastern wall completely open to the rain-slicked city below.

Standing a few paces away were two armed guards, eyeing him with lewd, mocking smirks as they nudged each other with their elbows. One of them began miming a crude, rhythmic pelvic thrust with a laugh, while the other puffed lazily on a cigarette, thoroughly entertained.

Realizing they were mocking his relationship with Il-hyun, Jakyeong ground his molars together, his eyes narrowing into razor slits.

"Where is Kang Il-hyun?"

The smoking guard strolled over, flicking his burning ash straight into Jakyeong’s face.

"Arrogant little bitch. You think President Kang is your schoolyard buddy?"

"I asked you where he is, you fucking roaches!"

The guard stepped into point-blank range, his hand dropping down to his belt buckle with a repulsive, sleazy sneer.

"Why don't you get on your knees and suck this off? If your technique is good enough, maybe I'll tell you."
